evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Jules moves straight from the time-box confirmation into discovery (move date, email, phone, addresses) with no 'what are your biggest concerns?' or parallel check.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Seven items largely covered: property type (one-bed, two-bed apartments), floors/stories (explicitly discussed — basement as first floor, main as second, one apartment has third level), number of rooms (one bedroom, two bedroom), walking distance (seven doors down on same street — effectively zero), additional stops (Washer/Dryer to different apartment level), special considerations (basement garage, three staircases between units, tight stairs in complex). evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not asked by Jules. Barbara volunteers 'We plan to pre pack all, all the small items' and mentions plastic bins, but Jules never asks or offers the packing service.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: No box count or overflow check offered.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Jules gives hourly rate ($102/hour per mover, $306 for three movers) and a range: '$765.18 to $918' for '2.5 to 3 hours.' Personalizes slightly to 'with the three guys the move will be a little bit quicker' and acknowledges prior hour-long move, but no explicit personalization tied to customer's stated concerns or prep level (e.g., 'since you're pre-packing, which saves time').

evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Jules never asks 'Does that feel fair?' or equivalent. No pause for confirmation after price quote.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No reflection back or confirmation that the Two Promises (if they had been delivered) addressed customer concerns.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Jules says 'Well I guess that's, oh' and then customer asks about square footage, and later Jules says 'Well I guess that's, oh' again — neither is a genuine 'What's still concerning you?' type check. At the very end, customer volunteers info about furniture type and minimalist daughter, but Jules never proactively asks 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Jules never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' or any equivalent ask for the business. Moves directly to 'I can get you scheduled right now' and confirms logistics without an explicit yes to the engagement itself.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Date (November 5th) ✓, phone number (1660 and daughter's ending in 1) ✓, arrival window (8:30–9 AM) ✓, crew size (three movers) ✓, addresses (from and to) ✓, notes for crew (only minimal mention of her being a minimalist with light furniture, no specific concerns captured for the crew) — largely confirmed but crew notes are thin.

top_strength: Jules gathered comprehensive logistics details (property type, floor layout, stair configurations, appliance placement, square footage) that would give the moving company a clear picture of the job complexity.
coaching_note: You skipped 'Their Agenda' entirely — jump straight from the time-box into probing without ever asking 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns?' This is the single highest-value move on the rubric and sets the tone for the entire call.
